summary_en: Asahi Kasei raised interim dividend to 24 yen per share from 22 yen, and revised full-year dividend guidance to 48 yen from 44 yen for fiscal year ending March 2027. The company targets DOE of 3% and progressive dividend growth based on medium-term free cash flow outlook.
title_en: Notice Regarding Interim Dividend Increase and Revision of Year-End Dividend Forecast
translation_en_brief:
On November 5, 2026, Asahi Kasei Corporation announced an increase in its interim dividend for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. The interim dividend per share was raised to 24 yen from the previously announced 22 yen, with an interim dividend total of 32,083 million yen. Simultaneously, the company revised its full-year dividend guidance upward to 48 yen per share from 44 yen, reflecting an increase of 2 yen in the year-end dividend to 24 yen.

The company stated that its dividend policy is guided by medium-term free cash flow projections. Under the Medium-Term Management Plan 2027 'Trailblaze Together' launched in fiscal 2025, the company targets a return on equity (DOE) of approximately 3% and pursues progressive dividend growth over the medium to long term to achieve continuous improvement in capital returns. The board of directors adopted this policy taking into account the financial position of the company for the fiscal year ending March 2027.

The dividend increase is supported by the company's forward-looking capital allocation strategy. The consolidated payout ratio is expected to remain at a sustainable level of 37.2% for fiscal 2027, compared to 35.9% for the previous year and 38.8% for fiscal 2025.
